chains.title: GATA2 binds the reference allele more strongly at the LMO1 enhancer and activates LMO1

links.claim: GATA2 binds the reference C allele more strongly than the alt A allele. GATA2 has its own QBiC-SELEX model and is strongly expressed in SK-N-SH (133.07 TPM, rank 17/1626); ENCODE ChIP-seq shows GATA2 occupancy over the variant in SK-N-SH. Its own model gives effect -0.816 (z -56.07), with ref at the 100th and alt at the 77.3rd percentile, so the ref allele is the stronger GATA2 site. GATA3 shares the motif but is lower-expressed and has a weaker allele-specific drop at this base, so GATA2 is the better-supported GATA factor.
The variant lies in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, and GATA2 ChIP-seq occupies this element over the variant in SK-N-SH.

The element is in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from the LMO1 TSS; fine-mapping/L2G links this credible set to LMO1, and the alt A allele is associated with lower LMO1 expression in GTEx skeletal muscle (NES -0.13), consistent with weakening a ref-preferring activator. Caveat: the eQTL tissue is skeletal muscle and the L2G sets are not neuroblastoma.
SK-N-SH is a neuroblastoma line in which this element is active, GATA2 is highly expressed, and GATA2 is bound over the variant, making the mechanism plausible in the relevant tumor-cell context.

LMO1 is implicated in neuroblastoma biology and can promote aggressive/migratory phenotypes. If GATA2 activates LMO1 through this enhancer, the alt A allele would lower LMO1 and reduce LMO1-driven phenotypes. This direction is inferred, not directly shown: no supplied evidence ties this allele to neuroblastoma risk.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP or reporter assays show ref C > alt A at this base.
The alt A allele reduces enhancer activity and LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH or other neuroblastoma cells.
GATA2 depletion reduces LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH.

The alt A allele does not reduce LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma cells.

chains.title: FOXJ3, via a paralog-mapped forkhead motif, binds the alt allele more strongly and may repress LMO1

links.claim: FOXJ3 is occupied over the variant in SK-N-SH and expressed there (26.62 TPM, rank 196/1626). The reported best QBiC-SELEX model is a CIS-BP-mapped FOXG1 model, not FOXJ3's own model, and it gives effect 0.65 (z 14.24), with alt at the 99.0th percentile: this supports alt-stronger binding only at paralog level. The allelic direction for FOXJ3 itself is therefore weaker than for GATA2.
The variant lies in the active dELS EH38E1518342, and FOXJ3 ChIP-seq occupies this element over the variant in SK-N-SH.

The element is in the LMO1 gene body near LMO1; L2G/fine-mapping links the credible set to LMO1, and the alt allele is associated with lower LMO1 expression in GTEx skeletal muscle. This direction fits only if FOXJ3 represses LMO1, which is not established.
FOXJ3 is expressed and bound at this active enhancer in SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells.

If FOXJ3 represses LMO1, the alt A allele's stronger FOXJ3 site would lower LMO1 and reduce LMO1-driven neuroblastoma phenotypes. The sign of FOXJ3 action and any allele-to-neuroblastoma link are missing from the supplied evidence, so this is an unproven inference.

predictions: Alt A increases FOXJ3 occupancy at this base in allele-specific ChIP or reporter assays.
FOXJ3 depletion reverses the alt-lower-LMO1 effect if FOXJ3 is the relevant repressor.
The alt allele changes LMO1 enhancer activity in a FOXJ3-site-dependent manner.
falsified_if: FOXJ3 binding is not allele-specific at this base.
The alt A allele does not increase FOXJ3 occupancy.
FOXJ3 depletion has no effect on LMO1 expression or on the allelic enhancer effect.

chains.title: GATA3, via its own GATA model, binds the reference allele more strongly and regulates LMO1

links.claim: GATA3 is occupied over the variant in SK-N-SH and expressed there (51.82 TPM, rank 80/1626). The GATA3 detail row provides its own GATA3 model in addition to the mapped GATA2 model: the own model gives effect -4.206 (z -54.11), with ref at the 99.9th and alt at the 97.4th percentile, so ref binds more strongly. The E21 'best model' line is a CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model and is not independent GATA3 evidence; the own-model row is what supports this chain, but GATA2 remains better supported overall because of higher expression and the larger alt-site loss.
The variant lies in the active dELS EH38E1518342, and GATA3 ChIP-seq occupies this element over the variant in SK-N-SH.

The element is in the LMO1 gene body near the LMO1 TSS; L2G/fine-mapping links the credible set to LMO1, and the alt A allele is associated with lower LMO1 expression in GTEx skeletal muscle, consistent with weakening a ref-preferring GATA activator. Caveat: the eQTL tissue is not neuroblastoma.
GATA3 is expressed and bound at this active enhancer in SK-N-SH neuroblastoma cells.

If GATA3 rather than GATA2 activates LMO1 at this element, the alt A allele would lower LMO1 and reduce LMO1-driven neuroblastoma phenotypes. The neuroblastoma-risk direction is not established by the supplied evidence.

predictions: GATA3-specific ChIP or reporter assays show ref C > alt A at this base.
GATA3 depletion reduces LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH, ideally more than GATA2 depletion.
The alt A allele lowers LMO1 enhancer activity in a GATA-motif-dependent manner.
falsified_if: GATA3 binding is not allele-specific at this base.
GATA2 depletion accounts for the LMO1 effect and GATA3 depletion does not.
The alt A allele does not alter LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma cells.

grades_v0.reason: Occupancy is shown by ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in the matching biosample SK-N-SH (E05, ENCSR706VOO), and the QBiC-SELEX change is from GATA2's own model in the stated direction (effect -0.816, z -56.07, ref binds more; ref 100th vs alt 77.3rd percentile = strong site) (E20). Both halves of the binding link are present. The GATA2-over-GATA3 choice is justified (own model vs CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model, 133 vs 52 TPM).

E03 places the variant inside EH38E1518342 (dELS) and E05/E20 show GATA2 occupancy over the variant in SK-N-SH. Minor caveat: the DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 z-scores in E03 are maxima over all ENCODE biosamples, so enhancer activity is not demonstrated specifically in SK-N-SH.

E02 places the variant in the LMO1 gene body; E16 gives L2G LMO1 0.92/PIP 1.00 for this credible set; E17 gives a significant GTEx eQTL for LMO1 (NES -0.13 for alt A). Direction is internally consistent (ref-preferring activator, alt lowers LMO1). Caveat: the eQTL tissue is skeletal muscle, not neuroblastoma, and L2G sets are for height/metabolites, not neuroblastoma.
The expression context is DepMap ACH-000149 = SK-N-SH; E04/E05/E20 show the element is bound by GATA2 and GATA2 is highly expressed (133 TPM, rank 17/1626) in exactly this line.

E18a supports a general oncogenic/aggressive role for LMO1 in neuroblastoma, but nothing cited ties this variant's allele to neuroblastoma risk or aggressiveness; the supplied GWAS hits (E15/E16) are metabolite, height and blood-pressure traits, not neuroblastoma. The claim that alt A 'would reduce aggressiveness' is an inference from the eQTL direction, openly flagged as not established.

Occupancy is supported (E06, 2 SK-N-SH peaks over the variant; 51.8 TPM). However the allelic change cited (E21, z -56.07, effect -0.816) is identical to GATA2's and comes from a CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model, i.e. one GATA factor's binding change used as evidence for another. That makes the allelic half of the link indirect at best; the chain itself concedes this.
E03 puts the variant in the dELS EH38E1518342 and E06 shows GATA3 occupancy over the variant in SK-N-SH; the element claim does not depend on the shared-model allelic change.
Same evidence as H1.gene: E02 gene-body location, E16 L2G LMO1 0.92, E17 LMO1 eQTL (NES -0.13 for alt). Direction consistent with a ref-preferring GATA activator.
E04/E06/E21 show GATA3 expressed (~52 TPM) and bound at this dELS in SK-N-SH, the stated neuroblastoma context.

As H1.phenotype: LMO1's oncogenic role in neuroblastoma is supported by E18a, but no evidence links this base, or GATA3 specifically, to neuroblastoma risk; the direction is asserted rather than shown.

Occupancy is supported (E07, 2 SK-N-SH peaks; 26.6 TPM). But the allelic change in E23 (z 14.24, effect 0.65, alt binds more) comes from FOXG1_NA, a CIS-BP-mapped paralog model, not FOXJ3's own model, even though the record says FOXJ3 has its own model in the collection. The alt-stronger direction therefore rests on a related TF's model - indirect evidence, so weak.
E03 places the variant in EH38E1518342 dELS and E07 shows FOXJ3 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in SK-N-SH.
E02 (LMO1 gene body), E16 (L2G LMO1 0.92), E17 (alt lowers LMO1, NES -0.13). Note the direction only fits if FOXJ3 represses, which is the unproven part.
E04/E07/E23 show FOXJ3 expressed and bound at this element in SK-N-SH.

The chain's phenotype direction depends entirely on an unevidenced assumption that FOXJ3 represses LMO1; E18a speaks only to LMO1 promoting neuroblastoma phenotypes, not to FOXJ3's sign of action. The chain acknowledges the sign ambiguity, so this is a plausible but unsupported inference.

checks.why: Establishes whether GATA3 has any independent model in the QBiC-SELEX collection or is only covered through the mapped GATA2 model; if only mapped, H2's allelic evidence collapses into H1's and H2 should drop well below 0.1.

Directly tests the Open Targets evidence linking LMO1 to neuroblastoma by evidence type (GWAS, somatic, expression, literature); this is the missing piece the phenotype links currently assert from a single macrophage-conditioned-medium quote.

Returns all GTEx v8 single-tissue eQTLs for this variant, not just skeletal muscle; if LMO1 eQTLs appear in neural or neuroblastoma-adjacent tissues with the same sign, the enhancer-to-LMO1 direction becomes context-relevant rather than a muscle-only observation, and if other genes (e.g. RIC3) show stronger, opposite-sign eQTLs the L2G assignment is contested.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr11:8233861:C>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000149), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 12 occupied (5 with a strong site), 5 of 115 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 30 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 529 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 2 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
